text:
**Refined prompt:** Answer three read-only questions about this NestJS RealWorld codebase from a source-of-truth stance — (1) does the comment-delete path compare the caller against the comment's author, (2) exactly which `ProfileController` routes `AuthMiddleware` is applied to, (3) what the `*RO` interface suffix denotes — with every claim cited to `file:line`, no edits, and gaps in what I read stated explicitly.

---

## 1. `deleteComment` — no, there is no ownership check

There is no line comparing the caller to the comment's author, because the caller's identity never enters the call path and no author is recorded on a comment.

**The handler never asks who is calling** — `src/article/article.controller.ts:84-88`:

```ts
@Delete(':slug/comments/:id')
async deleteComment(@Param() params) {
  const {slug, id} = params;
  return await this.articleService.deleteComment(slug, id);
}
```

No `@User('id')` parameter, unlike `favorite()` / `unFavorite()` two methods down (`article.controller.ts:94`, `:102`). Only `slug` and `id` reach the service.

**The service deletes purely by id** — `src/article/article.service.ts:114-129`. It loads the article by slug (`:115`), loads the comment by id (`:117`), finds it in `article.comments` (`:118`), splices and deletes (`:121-122`). The only predicate is `_comment.id === comment.id`. Nothing reads `req.user`.

**There is nothing to compare against anyway.** `Comment` has `id`, `body`, and a `@ManyToOne` back to the article — no author column or relation (`src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15`), and `addComment()` sets only `comment.body` before saving (`article.service.ts:104-105`). So even a check written today would have no owner field to read. This matches what `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` already lists as pending design work.

**What the route *does* enforce:** `AuthMiddleware` is applied to `articles/:slug/comments/:id` for `DELETE` (`src/article/article.module.ts:29`), so an anonymous caller gets 401. That is authentication only — any logged-in user can delete any comment on any article. The `@ApiResponse({ status: 403, description: 'Forbidden.' })` at `article.controller.ts:83` documents a check that isn't implemented.

Two adjacent behaviours I noticed while reading (not run, inferred from the code): a comment id that doesn't exist makes `commentRepository.findOne(id)` return `undefined`, and `comment.id` inside the `findIndex` callback (`article.service.ts:118`) would then throw a `TypeError` → 500 on any article that has comments; and a comment id belonging to a *different* article falls to the `else` at `:125-126`, returning 200 with the article and deleting nothing.

## 2. Profile routes with the auth middleware

One entry only — `src/profile/profile.module.ts:20-22`:

```ts
consumer
  .apply(AuthMiddleware)
  .forRoutes({path: 'profiles/:username/follow', method: RequestMethod.ALL});
```

`RequestMethod.ALL` means it covers both handlers on that path:

| Route (global prefix `api`, `src/main.ts:8`) | Handler | Guarded |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `follow()` — `profile.controller.ts:23-26` | ✅ |
| `DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow` | `unFollow()` — `profile.controller.ts:28-31` | ✅ |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `getProfile()` — `profile.controller.ts:18-21` | ❌ public |

`getProfile()` is worth calling out: it's unguarded but still takes `@User('id')`. With no middleware to set `req.user`, the decorator falls through to decoding the `Authorization` header itself (`src/user/user.decorator.ts:12-17`) and returns `undefined` when no token is sent — so the route works anonymously and `profile.service.ts:43-45` simply omits the `following` flag when `id` is falsy. Optional identity, not a guard.

## 3. What `RO` means

**Response Object** — it marks the interface as the RealWorld response *envelope* rather than the payload itself. Every RealWorld frontend reads `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, so the wrapper key is part of the API contract:

- `UserRO { user: UserData }` — `src/user/user.interface.ts:9-11`
- `ProfileRO { profile: ProfileData }` — `src/profile/profile.interface.ts:8-10`
- `ArticleRO { article }`, `ArticlesRO { articles, articlesCount }`, `CommentsRO { comments }` — `src/article/article.interface.ts:20-31`

Request bodies mirror the same nesting on the way in — handlers read `@Body('article')` / `@Body('comment')` (`article.controller.ts:52`, `:60`, `:77`).

Two caveats visible in the source:

- `ArticleRO.article` is typed as the raw `ArticleEntity` (`article.interface.ts:25`), **not** the spec-shaped `ArticleData` declared just above it at `:7-18`. So the `favorited` / `favoritesCount` / `createdAt` fields that interface promises are never actually produced — the entity's own column names go out instead. That's the conformance work in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`.
- The suffix is a convention, not an enforced one. `ArticleController.create()` has no return-type annotation (`article.controller.ts:52`) and forwards `ArticleService.create()`, which is typed `Promise<ArticleEntity>` and returns `newArticle` bare (`article.service.ts:170`, `:186`) — no `{ article }` wrapper. `LESSONS.md:49-57` records this as a fixed bug (#57); in the code I read, it is still unwrapped.

I read the controllers, modules, interfaces, `comment.entity.ts`, `user.decorator.ts`, `main.ts`, `profile.service.ts:1-60`, and `article.service.ts:87-195`. I did not read `auth.middleware.ts`, `user.service.ts`, or the `prisma/` folder (flagged as a non-production experiment in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24`).
